provenance.publicationTitle: Scottish Income Tax rates and bands
provenance.methodologyNotes: UKMR-controlled transcription; Scottish Government SRC-013 remains Scottish policy provenance. Operational confirmation reviewed at 2026-09-14T14:41:18Z: GOV.UK Income Tax in Scotland: Current rates (https://www.gov.uk/scottish-income-tax) confirms all six 2026/27 bands on the same published income basis; HMRC Rates and thresholds for employers 2026 to 2027 (https://www.gov.uk/guidance/rates-and-thresholds-for-employers-2026-to-2027, Scotland tax table) corroborates the top rate above GBP 125140. The HMRC current-and-previous-years page (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/rates-and-allowances-income-tax/income-tax-rates-and-allowances-current-and-past) currently says Over GBP 125141 after an advanced band ending at GBP 125140. Under the locked UKMR resolution, this is an official-source presentation inconsistency, not policy-rule ambiguity: use advanced through GBP 125140 inclusive and top above GBP 125140 exclusive, continuous with the preceding band and corroborated by current operational sources. The operational pages were reviewed as HTML, not retained; no original-content checksum is claimed. No liability calculation or threshold derivation.
limitations: The Scottish Government policy page still labels the table proposed; it is retained as policy provenance, not used alone as final operational confirmation. Current GOV.UK Scottish rates confirm all six bands; HMRC employer guidance corroborates the top boundary.

thresholdBasis=published_income_with_standard_allowance means income before deducting Personal Allowance, as illustrated by the current GOV.UK Scottish table; not taxable-income bounds after allowances. HMRC after-allowances bands use a different presentation and are not mixed into these rows.

The HMRC current-and-previous-years page says Over GBP 125141; current GOV.UK/HMRC operational sources say over/Above GBP 125140. UKMR uses GBP 125140 under the locked presentation-inconsistency resolution recorded in methodologyNotes.
Personal Allowance, taper and zero point remain separate reference rules sourced to HMRC SRC-011.
